concept.name: Opening auction
concept.definition: The call auction that establishes a security's official opening price at the start of regular trading, concentrating overnight and on-open orders into a single-price cross before continuous trading begins.
concept.intuition: All the demand that built up since the last close is pooled and cleared at one price, which becomes the day's official open.
concept.mechanics: Venues accept market-on-open and limit-on-open orders until a cutoff (on Nasdaq, 9:28 a.m. ET), disseminate indicative clearing prices and imbalance information, then at 9:30 a.m. cross the opening book against the continuous book at the price that maximizes paired shares; the result sets the official opening price.
concept.failure_modes: Overnight news can make the opening cross highly volatile and one-sided; if few orders participate, the opening price can gap far from the prior close and immediately trigger volatility safeguards such as LULD.
concept.misconceptions: The opening price is not a continuation of the pre-market price and not a consensus fair value — it is the output of one matching process at one instant, and heavy imbalance can make it an outlier.
concept.example: After earnings released overnight, a stock's Opening Cross on Nasdaq clears at $102.40 versus a $95.00 prior close, and that cross price becomes the Nasdaq Official Opening Price.

citations.source: Nasdaq, The Nasdaq Opening and Closing Crosses FAQ
